title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. T_0 = V(I) ⊂ T is a first-order (square-zero) thickening. X_0/T_0 is smooth (the margin says a relative, possibly formal, smooth scheme). X' and X'' are two smooth liftings of X_0 to T, with X'×_T T_0 ≅ X_0 ≅ X''×_T T_0. All sheaves live on the common underlying space |X_0| = |X'| = |X''|.

The torsor and its group. P is the sheaf of germs of T-isomorphisms X' → X'' inducing the identity on X_0. G is the sheaf of germs of T-automorphisms of X'' inducing the identity on X_0.
- Since I^2 = 0 and X''/T is flat, such an automorphism has the form id + D. Here D is a T-derivation O_{X''} → I·O_{X''} = f_0^*(I), so it factors through Ω^1_{X_0/T_0}.
- Hence G ≅ Hom(Ω^1_{X_0/T_0}, f_0^*I) = V_{X_0/T_0} ⊗ f_0^*I. This is a sheaf of abelian groups, a twisted tangent sheaf.
- P is a right G-torsor. It is locally non-empty because smooth liftings are locally isomorphic.
- The margin note says that what is really used is only that X' and X'' are locally T-isomorphic over X_0; smoothness enters only through this.

Action on de Rham complexes. Functoriality of the relative de Rham complex gives:
- u : P → Hom of complexes (Ω•_{X'/T}, Ω•_{X''/T}) = Z^0 Hom•. Each u(p) is an isomorphism of dg-algebras.
- v : G → Aut(Ω•_{X''/T}).
- k : G → Hom^{-1}(Ω•_{X''/T}, Ω•_{X''/T}), given by interior product with the derivation D_g.
These satisfy two relations:
- u(pg) = u(p)v(g) (composition order by convention).
- v(g) − id = d k(g) + k(g) d. With I^2 = 0 one has g^* = id + L_{D_g}, so this is exactly Cartan's homotopy formula L_D = d i_D + i_D d.

What it is for. Any two local identifications X' ≅ X'' induce maps on de Rham complexes that differ by an explicit, G-additive homotopy. So they glue to a canonical isomorphism Ω•_{X'/T} ≅ Ω•_{X''/T} in the derived category of |X_0| (compatible with the algebra structure), hence a canonical isomorphism H_dR(X'/T) ≅ H_dR(X''/T). Applied to the two pullbacks of a family along the two projections of the first infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal of the base, this yields the Gauss–Manin connection. This is the 'crystalline' construction of the canonical connection, and the title of the page says exactly this.

Next page. Grothendieck abstracts the gluing as a lemma in homological algebra. Given complexes K', K'' on a ringed space, an abelian sheaf G, a right G-torsor P, and data u, v, h with the same identities, one obtains a morphism K' → K'' in the derived category. The device is the extension 0 → G → Ḡ → Z → 0 whose fibre over 1 is P, and the two-term complex L = [G → Ḡ] in degrees 0 and 1, which is quasi-isomorphic to Z. Presumably u, v, h assemble into a morphism L ⊗ K' → K'', or into Hom•(K', K'').
errors: Composition/variance conventions are left implicit. If u(p) is pushforward of forms (p^{-1})^*, then u(pg) = u(p)v(g) only holds with pg read as g∘p and composition read diagrammatically. This is harmless.
On the next page the relation is written u(g) = dh(g) + h(g)d. It should be v(g) − id = dh(g) + h(g)d, as on this page.
On the next page h is typed G → Hom^{-1}(K', K''). By analogy with this page it should be Hom^{-1}(K'', K'') (or one composes with u(p)).

The margin claim that smoothness of X_0, X', X'' is needed only for local isomorphy is not quite the whole story. The identification G ≅ V_{X_0/T_0} ⊗ f_0^*I also uses flatness of X''/T and the square-zero hypothesis, though not smoothness per se.

ideas.what: Smooth liftings over a square-zero thickening are locally isomorphic; the isomorphisms form a torsor under T_{X_0/T_0} ⊗ f_0^*I
ideas.modern_name: Deformation theory of smooth schemes: torsor of liftings / isomorphisms of liftings

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism of de Rham complexes of two liftings, via Cartan homotopy formula for automorphisms id + D
ideas.modern_name: Independence of the lifting / de Rham cohomology is a crystal; crystalline construction of the Gauss–Manin connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck ('Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', IHES 1966, notes by Coates–Jussila); Katz–Oda 1968; Berthelot 1974
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968), 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'

ideas.what: Abstract gluing lemma: a G-torsor of chain maps with additive homotopies yields a derived-category morphism, using the extension Ḡ of Z by G attached to P and the complex [G → Ḡ] ≃ Z
ideas.modern_name: Twisting by a torsor via its associated extension class in Ext^1(Z, G) = H^1(G); descent of morphisms up to coherent homotopy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; the torsor/extension correspondence goes back to Grothendieck (Tôhoku, SGA 7 / SGA 4) and Giraud; Čech-style versions in Katz–Oda and Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Torsor–extension dictionary in SGA 7 Exp. VII (Grothendieck); this specific gluing lemma: unsure

missed.claim: A Čech-free construction of the canonical de Rham comparison isomorphism. One packages the torsor P of local isomorphisms into an extension Ḡ of Z by G and a two-term complex quasi-isomorphic to Z, then builds the derived-category morphism directly. Standard accounts (Katz–Oda, Berthelot, Berthelot–Ogus) use Čech coverings or the linearization/PD-envelope formalism instead. The device is elegant but close to folklore.
missed.quote: On introduit l'extension Ḡ de Z par G ... définie en termes de P par la relation g^{-1}(1) ≃ P
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a canonical, choice-free (Čech-free) gluing of local homotopy data. This fits modern ∞-categorical descent. It also makes the compatibility with Γ(O_X)-structures and relativization (noted on the next page) transparent.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is the standard crystalline construction of the Gauss–Manin connection, which Grothendieck himself published in 'Crystals' (1966/68). The only mildly distinctive element is the abstract torsor/extension gluing lemma begun on the next page. It is a neat formulation but close to folklore.
transcription_corrections: Margin note on the left reads roughly 'conditions de lissité de X_0, X', X'' résulte de X', X'' point loc. T-isom. (sur X_0)'. The sense is that smoothness is used only through local isomorphy of the liftings.
Under T_0 ↪ T: 'immersion 1-nilpotente' (i.e. I^2 = 0) is correct.
Margin by the arrow from X_0 (the f_0 arrow): 'schéma relatif formel lisse' appears to be right.
'P un G-torseur à droite' replaces the struck-out 'faisceau principal homogène à droite sur G'.
Struck-out words: 'Isom de complexes' corrected to 'Hom de complexes', and 'Aut de complexes' with 'Aut' partly struck; the text in brackets on the page.
